visible.presentation_text:
Consult request from the facility's licensed wildlife rehabilitator.

Red-tailed hawk, hatch-year, admitted six weeks ago after a vehicle strike. Right ulna and radius fracture, closed, stabilized. Fracture has healed with malunion at approximately 30 degrees; the wing has limited extension and the bird cannot achieve sustained flight. Two flight-pen evaluations at 3 and 6 weeks post-removal: no lift, no altitude gain.

Bird is maintaining weight at 1,190 g, self-feeding on whole prey, casting normally, alert and responsive to approach, perching and moving between low perches without difficulty. No pain behaviors observed; no analgesia currently indicated. Attending veterinarian assessed quality of life as acceptable across all Five Domains with the exception of behavioral interactions, noting the bird remains stress-reactive to handling after six weeks.

Bird is non-releasable. Educational placement has been sought: three permitted facilities in the region were contacted, all report full raptor rosters and no capacity through next year. The bird's stress reactivity makes it a poor candidate for a program bird regardless. No breeding or research placement applies to this species.

Permanent captivity would require a dedicated flight enclosure, daily whole-prey feeding, and routine veterinary care. Estimated 15–20 year captive lifespan. Facility currently holds two permanent education birds at capacity.

The caller mentions the bird has unusually pale plumage.
menu_options: Continue care while the placement search continues
Transfer the animal to another rehabilitation facility
Request an extension of holding authorization
